mainTopic: A minor betrothed without her father: the widow sold as a maidservant, the girl who falls to יבום, and a betrothal over a cup of wine
overview: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא that lets a father sell his young daughter as a maidservant even to a כהן she may not marry, such as an אלמנה to a כהן גדול. It asks how such a girl could be a widow and still be sold, and suggests this proves that a minor's self-betrothal counts, against עולא. רב עמרם answers that she became a widow through קידושי יעוד, following רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. Next comes רב's ruling about a minor betrothed without her father whose husband died, leaving her for יבום. If the brother did מאמר, she needs a גט, חליצה, and מיאון, each covering a different doubt about which betrothal her father agreed to. If he did not do מאמר, she needs only חליצה. מיאון is not needed then, because everyone knows a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only מדרבנן, as ריש לקיש teaches. Finally, a story of two men betrothing their children over a cup of wine leads to a ruling by רבינא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: she may be sold even to a forbidden כהן
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that both sides agree a father may sell his daughter as a maidservant to a כהן גדול even if she is an אלמנה, or to a regular כהן even if she is a גרושה or חלוצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they agree that he may sell her as a widow to a High Priest, and as a divorcée or a חלוצה to a regular priest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of a ברייתא. This line is the setup for the question the גמרא is about to ask.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול may not marry an אלמנה, and a regular כהן may not marry a גרושה or חלוצה. Still, such marriages do take effect, so the father may sell her to them. The key word for the coming question is 'אלמנה': how did this young girl become a widow?

keyTerms.meaning: And they agree (both opinions in the ברייתא)
A widow
The High Priest, who may not marry a widow
A woman released from יבום through חליצה
A regular כהן

phrases.english: And they agree that he may sell her
phrases.notes: 'They' means the two opinions argued about earlier in this ברייתא; 'sell her' means as a maidservant.

phrases.english: as a widow to a High Priest,
as a divorcée or a חלוצה to a regular priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא begun before this section, which the גמרא will now examine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A father may sell his daughter as a maidservant even to a כהן whom she may not marry, such as an אלמנה to a כהן גדול.

steps.title: What kind of widow is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this girl became a widow. It rules out the idea that her father betrothed her, because a father cannot sell his daughter as a maidservant after he has married her off.
steps.simpleTranslation: This widow, what is the case? If you say her father betrothed her, can he still sell her? But a person cannot sell his daughter into servitude after marriage!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means when it calls the girl an אלמנה. It tests the most obvious answer and shows it cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father may only sell his daughter as a maidservant while she is young. If he had betrothed her, she would leave his power to sell, since there is no selling into servitude after אישות. So the simple explanation fails, and the גמרא is setting up its next move.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
If you say (offering a possible answer to test it)
Servitude as a maidservant
Marriage, including betrothal

phrases.english: This widow, what is the case?
If you say that her father betrothed her,
is he able to sell her?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין אָדָם מוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ
phrases.english: But a person does not sell his daughter
into servitude after marriage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines the word 'אלמנה' in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case of 'widow' can the ברייתא mean, if the father could still sell her afterward?

steps.title: So it must be a girl who betrothed herself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the case must be a girl who betrothed herself without her father, and the ברייתא still calls her a widow. That would mean her self-betrothal counted, which is a challenge to עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it that she betrothed herself, and the ברייתא still calls her a widow!
steps.whatsHappening: Since the father did not betroth her, the גמרא says she must have betrothed herself. Calling her a 'widow' shows her betrothal was real, which challenges the view of עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If her own betrothal did not count, she would not be a widow at all. Because her father did not accept this betrothal, she is still in his power, and he can sell her. So the ברייתא seems to prove that a minor's self-betrothal has some effect, against עולא, who says it means nothing without the father.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't it that (pushing toward a conclusion)
She betrothed herself

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it that she betrothed herself,
and it calls her a widow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having ruled out a father's betrothal, the גמרא lands on self-betrothal and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's view that a minor who betrothed herself without her father has no betrothal at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls her an אלמנה. That is only possible if her self-betrothal took effect.

steps.title: The case is a betrothal of יעוד
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם, quoting רבי יצחק, says the ברייתא speaks of a קידושי יעוד, following רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. In his view the original sale money was not given for betrothal, so the father never betrothed her and may sell her again.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב עמרם said in the name of רבי יצחק: Here it is speaking of a betrothal of designation, following רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who said the original money was not given for betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב עמרם answers the challenge with a different case. The girl was sold as an אמה עבריה, her master designated her as his wife (יעוד), and he died, so she is a widow without having betrothed herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one would think the father's sale money counts as his betrothal of her, so he could not sell her again. But רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds the first money was only for the sale, not for betrothal. So the father never betrothed her, he may sell her again, and the ברייתא gives no proof against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal of designation: a master marries the maidservant he bought
According to the opinion of
The original money paid for the maidservant
Were given

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Amram said that Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Here it is dealing with a betrothal of designation.
phrases.notes: She was sold as a maidservant, her master chose her as his wife, and then he died.

phrases.english: And it follows Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda,
who said: The original money
was not given for betrothal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב עַמְרָם אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק הָכָא בְּקִידּוּשֵׁי יִעוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by offering another case where she is a widow but her father may still sell her.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The only way she could be a widow and still be sold is if she betrothed herself, so self-betrothal works.
steps.terutzMaskana: She became a widow through יעוד, and per רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה her father never betrothed her, so the ברייתא proves nothing against עולא.
steps.whatToRemember: The 'widow' in the ברייתא is a maidservant whose master designated her and died, not a girl who betrothed herself. The challenge to עולא is answered.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the father 'married her off' through the sale. According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, the sale money was only for the sale, so the betrothal of יעוד was never the father's betrothal.

steps.title: רב: she refuses his מאמר but not his זיקה
steps.stepSummary: A new statement: if the man who betrothed her died and she fell to his brother for יבום, רב says she does מיאון against the brother's מאמר, but not against the יבום bond itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: If he died and she fell before his brother for יבום, רב הונא said in the name of רב: She refuses his מאמר, but she does not refuse his זיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a ruling of רב. It deals with the same young girl betrothed without her father, whose husband then died, leaving her for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מאמר is a betrothal by the brother-in-law, done with money like a regular betrothal. רב says מיאון applies to that מאמר, but the bond of יבום itself (זיקה) is not undone by מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (an opinion of later rabbis)
Marriage of a widow to her dead husband's brother
She refuses: a minor leaves her marriage through מיאון
Betrothal of a יבמה by the brother-in-law, using money
The bond between a יבמה and her brother-in-law

phrases.english: It was stated: If he died
phrases.notes: 'He' is the man who betrothed the young girl without her father's agreement.

phrases.english: and she fell before his brother for levirate marriage,
Rav Huna said that Rav said:
She refuses his levirate betrothal,
but she does not refuse his levirate bond.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר מֵת וְנָפְלָה לִפְנֵי אָחִיו לְיִבּוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new statement about the same kind of girl, now in a case of יבום.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor who fell to יבום does מיאון against the brother's מאמר, but not against the זיקה.

steps.title: How so? After מאמר she needs three things
steps.stepSummary: רב spells out his ruling: if the brother did מאמר with her, she needs a גט, חליצה, and מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? If he did מאמר with her, she needs a גט, she needs חליצה, and she needs מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains what his short rule means in practice. Once the brother has done מאמר, she must get all three: a גט, חליצה, and מיאון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the three handles a different doubt about whose betrothal her father agreed to. The גמרא will now explain each one.

keyTerms.meaning: How so?
A bill of divorce
The ceremony that releases a יבמה from יבום
Refusal: a minor leaving a marriage made under the rabbis' rules

phrases.english: How so? If he performed levirate betrothal with her,
she needs a bill of divorce, and she needs חליצה,
and she needs refusal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical meaning of רב's rule from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After מאמר, she needs a גט, חליצה, and מיאון.

steps.title: Why a גט and why חליצה
steps.stepSummary: She needs a גט in case her father agreed only to the second betrothal (the brother's). She needs חליצה in case her father agreed to the first betrothal, which would make her a real יבמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: She needs a גט, because perhaps the father agreed to the second betrothal. She needs חליצה, because perhaps the father agreed to the first betrothal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first two requirements. Each one covers a different possibility of which betrothal the father agreed to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father agreed to the brother's מאמר but not to the first man's betrothal, she was never a יבמה, so the מאמר is a normal betrothal and needs a גט. If the father agreed to the first betrothal, she is a real יבמה and needs חליצה to be freed.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps (a doubt we must cover)
Agreed, was satisfied with

phrases.english: She needs a bill of divorce,
since perhaps the father agreed to the betrothal of the second.
phrases.notes: The 'second' is the brother who did מאמר; the 'first' is the man who died.

phrases.english: She needs חליצה,
since perhaps the father agreed to the betrothal of the first.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָה גֵּט שֶׁמָּא נִתְרַצָּה הָאָב בְּקִידּוּשֵׁי שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasons for the first two of the three requirements.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does she need a גט and why does she need חליצה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גט covers the chance the father agreed only to the brother's betrothal; חליצה covers the chance he agreed to the first man's betrothal.

steps.title: Why she also needs מיאון
steps.stepSummary: She needs מיאון in case the father agreed to neither betrothal. Without it, people would think the betrothals were real and say that a betrothal does not take hold with her sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: She needs מיאון, because perhaps the father agreed neither to the first betrothal nor to the second, and people will say betrothal does not take hold with her sister.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third requirement. מיאון shows everyone that her betrothals were not full, real ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the father agreed to neither betrothal, she was never truly married to either man. If she only received a גט and חליצה, people would think she was really this man's wife. Then, if he later betrothed her sister, they would think that betrothal does not take hold, and might let the sister marry someone else without a גט. The מיאון shows that her betrothal was only by the rabbis' rules.

keyTerms.meaning: Take hold, take effect
Her sister
And people will say (a concern about public mistakes)

phrases.english: She needs refusal,
since perhaps the father did not agree
neither to the betrothal of the first
nor to the betrothal of the second,
and people will say that betrothal does not take hold with her sister.
phrases.notes: Without מיאון, people would think she was fully married to him. Then, if he betrothed her sister, they would wrongly think that betrothal does not count.

steps.triggerLanguage: צְרִיכָה מֵיאוּן שֶׁמָּא לֹא נִתְרַצָּה הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the third requirement, completing רב's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does she need מיאון in addition to a גט and חליצה?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In case the father agreed to neither betrothal; the מיאון stops people from thinking the betrothals were real and wrongly forbidding her sister.
steps.whatToRemember: Three doubts mean three requirements: a גט (maybe the father agreed only to the brother), חליצה (maybe he agreed to the first man), and מיאון (maybe he agreed to neither, so people should not think she was truly married).

steps.title: Without the brother's betrothal, only release from levirate marriage is needed
steps.stepSummary: רב finishes his ruling. If the brother did not do מאמר with her, she needs only חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not do מאמר with her, she needs only חליצה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second half of רב's ruling. If the brother never did מאמר, she needs only חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a מאמר, there is no second betrothal to worry about, so no גט is needed. The only doubt left is whether her father agreed to the first betrothal. If he did, she is a real יבמה and needs חליצה. If he did not, she is free anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothal-like act the brother does with his brother's widow before יבום
The ceremony that releases a widow from יבום
Only, alone

phrases.english: If he did not do levirate betrothal with her,
phrases.notes: "He" is the dead man's brother, the one she fell to for יבום.

phrases.english: she needs only חליצה, nothing more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other half of רב's ruling: the case with no מאמר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With no מאמר, only חליצה is required.

steps.title: Should refusal be required here too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether she should also need מיאון, so people will not think a betrothal cannot take hold with her sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: What would you say: she should also need מיאון, or else people will say that a betrothal does not take hold with her sister?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings up a possible objection. In step 8, מיאון was required so people would not draw a wrong conclusion about her sister. Why not here too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she is released with חליצה alone, people may think she was a real יבמה, and so a real חלוצה. Then they might think the brother cannot betroth her sister, as if that were a Torah-level ban. מיאון would show that the first betrothal was never fully real.

keyTerms.meaning: Refusal; a minor girl's way of ending a marriage set up by the Rabbis
Take hold, take effect (said of a betrothal)
If you would say; introduces a possible objection

phrases.english: What would you say?
She should also need מיאון,
or else people will say
that a betrothal does not take hold with her sister?
phrases.notes: He means the brother who did חליצה betrothing her sister.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the concern from step 8 does not also require מיאון here.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why is מיאון not required here, given the concern that people will make a mistake about her sister?

steps.title: Everyone knows the חלוצה's sister is only rabbinically forbidden
steps.stepSummary: There is no need for מיאון, because everyone knows that the sister of a חלוצה is forbidden only מדרבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Everyone knows that the sister of a חלוצה is forbidden only מדרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. No one will make the mistake we worried about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A betrothal does take hold with a woman forbidden only מדרבנן. Since everyone knows that אחות חלוצה is only a rabbinic ban, they know a betrothal with her would be valid anyway. So there is no wrong conclusion to prevent, and מיאון is not needed. In step 8 it was different: after the brother's מאמר she also received a גט, and the sister of a גרושה (אחות גרושה) is forbidden by Torah law, as the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: The sister of a woman one did חליצה with
Forbidden by rabbinic law, not Torah law
Everyone knows

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a rabbinic ban makes a betrothal fail. A betrothal still takes hold with a woman forbidden only מדרבנן. That is exactly why no mistake can happen here.

phrases.english: Everyone knows
that the sister of a חלוצה is forbidden only by rabbinic law.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since everyone knows a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only מדרבנן, they know a betrothal with her takes hold, so no mistake will happen and מיאון is not needed.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's source: divorcée's sister is Torah-forbidden, חלוצה's sister is rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up its answer with ריש לקיש, who says a משנה teaches that a divorcée's sister is forbidden by Torah law and a חלוצה's sister by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: As ריש לקיש said: Here רבי taught that the sister of a divorcée is forbidden by Torah law, and the sister of a חלוצה is forbidden by rabbinic law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the claim in step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש reads a משנה as drawing a clear line. The sister of one's divorced wife is a Torah ban, but the sister of one's חלוצה is only a rabbinic ban. This supports step 11's point that a חלוצה's sister is only rabbinically forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
The sister of one's divorced wife
By Torah law
From the words of the Sages, meaning rabbinic law

steps.whatToRemember: With no מאמר, only חליצה is needed. מיאון is not added, because a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only מדרבנן, so a betrothal with her takes hold anyway and no one will be misled.

phrases.english: As ריש לקיש said:
Here רבי taught
phrases.notes: רבי is רבי יהודה הנשיא. "Here" is a משנה in יבמות 41a.

phrases.english: that the sister of a divorcée is forbidden by Torah law,
and the sister of a חלוצה is forbidden by the words of the Sages.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כָּאן שָׁנָה רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the claim made in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That a חלוצה's sister is forbidden only מדרבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: ריש לקיש's reading of the משנה in יבמות 41a

steps.title: A betrothal made over a cup of wine
steps.stepSummary: A new story: two men drinking wine in בבל. One hands the other a cup of wine and says, "Your daughter is betrothed to my son."
steps.simpleTranslation: There were two men drinking wine under poplar trees in בבל. One of them took a cup of wine and gave it to his friend. He said: Your daughter is betrothed to my son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a real-life case. It is setting up a question about whether this betrothal counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a father gives the betrothal item on behalf of his son, and the girl's father receives it for his daughter. The story itself gives no ruling yet. It sets up the discussion that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: A cup of wine
Poplar trees
Is betrothed

phrases.english: There were two men
who were drinking wine
under poplar trees in Babylonia.
One of them took a cup of wine
and gave it to his friend.
He said: Your daughter is betrothed to me for my son.
phrases.notes: He means the friend is accepting the cup as a betrothal for his daughter to marry the speaker's son.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ בֵּי תְרֵי דַּהֲווֹ קָא שָׁתוּ חַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new case. רבינא's ruling on it (next step) uses the same worry, 'perhaps the father agreed' (שמא נתרצה האב), that drove רב's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet; this lays out the case of a betrothal made by fathers over a cup of wine.

steps.title: רבינא begins his ruling on the wine-cup case
steps.stepSummary: רבינא opens: "Even according to the one who says we worry that perhaps the father agreed..." His statement continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Even according to the one who says we are concerned that perhaps the father agreed...
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא starts to rule on the wine-cup case. The sentence is not finished yet, so this step only sets up his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבינא refers to the view, used earlier in the סוגיא, that when a young girl was betrothed without her father, we worry he may later have agreed to it. The word "even" shows he is about to argue that this worry may not apply in the new case, but his reason comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: A late אמורא from בבל
We are concerned, we take into account
Agreed, was willing

phrases.english: רבינא said:
Even according to the one who says
we are concerned that perhaps the father agreed—

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רָבִינָא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר חָיְישִׁינַן שֶׁמָּא נִתְרַצָּה הָאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins רבינא's ruling on the case in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet complete. רבינא is setting up a contrast with the view that we worry the father agreed.
